endorsements.name: David Endler
endorsements.label: Web Application Brute Forcing 101 - "Enemy of the State (Mechanism)"
endorsements.description: This presentation focuses on the ease with which many web application Session IDs can be brute-forced, allowing an attacker to hijack a legitimate web user's online session (e.g. Slashdot, Apache, Register.com, PHPNuke, etc.). While a somewhat narrow area of web application security, the simplicity of the attacks and the prevalence of these vulnerabilities on the Internet make this an important topic. Malicious users can easily try (usually automated) combinations of well-known usernames and passwords, or indeed attempt all possible combinations of the accepted Session ID character set. However, the scope of a brute force attack can be greatly reduced when Session IDs are predictable in nature. The presentation will include an overview of the issues involved in exploiting predictable or "reverse-engineerable" Session IDs in popular web applications, including a demonstration with several real-world exploitation examples. It will conclude with a description of techniques both users and web developers can use to protect against these types of attacks.
